title: Juniper and the Autopsy
premise: Estate lawyer Mirabel Halloran is summoned to read the will of Cordelia Voss, a reclusive heiress who died three days before her thirtieth anniversary dinner. The will names a beneficiary no one has heard of—Juniper—and encloses a confession letter postmarked after Cordelia's death, admitting to a drowning thirty years ago that Mirabel realizes was never investigated. As Mirabel traces Juniper's identity through forged records and the surviving dinner guests' interlocking alibis, he discovers Cordelia staged her own death to force the truth into the open, and that the letter's true author is still alive and watching him. At the anniversary dinner, rebuilt as a reenactment, the killer among the guests is exposed when the alibis collapse against tide charts Cordelia hid in the will's codicil; Mirabel survives an attempt on his life, delivers the confession to the drowned man's daughter—Juniper—and chooses to stop being the invisible man who files papers for the powerful.
about_author: Rafael Villalobos spent a decade as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, where he developed a reputation for mysteries built from paperwork, inheritance law, and the lies families tell to keep their money clean. He lives in a converted boathouse and claims he still reads strangers' wills for pleasure.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Mirabel Halloran, POV. Called to Voss House to read Cordelia Voss's will, Mirabel finds a document dated after her death, naming an unknown beneficiary, 'Juniper,' and sealed with instructions only he may open. The family bristles; the housekeeper flinches at his questions. Emotional beat: unease—the paper trail Mirabel trusts begins contradicting itself.

chapters.title: Postmarked After the Funeral
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. A confession letter arrives describing a drowning at the original anniversary dinner thirty years ago—a death with no police record. Mirabel cross-checks probate archives and finds the victim erased from every record. Emotional beat: dread deepening into obsession as he realizes someone engineered the erasure.

chapters.title: Five Glasses Raised
chapters.summary: Mirabel interviews the five surviving dinner guests: Cordelia's brother Ambrose, her business partner Lena, the retired doctor Pell, the gardener Sutter, and Cordelia herself—or so they claim. Each alibi is polished, rehearsed, identical in its gaps. Emotional beat: the cold elegance of coordinated silence.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Following the name, he finds Wren Okafor, the drowned man's daughter, raised under an assumed identity and paid anonymously for thirty years. She doesn't know who sent the money or why. Emotional beat: grief meeting anger—Wren wants answers, not charity, and becomes Mirabel's reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart Codicil
chapters.summary: Mirabel deciphers the will's codicil: tide tables and a seating diagram from the night of the drowning, proving one alibi is physically impossible. Before he can act, his office is ransacked and the codicil copy stolen. Emotional beat: the case turns predatory—he is no longer reading the past, it is reading him.

chapters.title: What Cordelia Bought
chapters.summary: Wren and Mirabel trace the anonymous payments to a shell company controlled by Ambrose Voss, who admits paying hush money but insists Cordelia orchestrated everything—including, perhaps, her own death. Emotional beat: vertigo; the confession letter may be bait, and Cordelia may have died to spring a trap.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Silence
chapters.summary: Housekeeper POV shift. Agnes reveals she saw the drowning as a young maid and was paid to forget; Cordelia hired her decades later as a living witness. She gives Mirabel Cordelia's final instruction: host the anniversary dinner again, same guests, same seats. Emotional beat: complicity and the terrible cost of staying silent to survive.

chapters.title: Invitations
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. He sends the invitations. The guests react like animals scenting fire—Lena offers him money, Pell offers threats dressed as concern, Sutter simply vanishes. Someone follows Wren home. Emotional beat: rising dread as the trap closes on everyone, including its architect's ghost.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Climax. At the reenacted dinner, Mirabel lays out the tide chart: only one guest could have reached the boathouse that night—Lena, whose partnership with Cordelia masked a theft and a murder Cordelia discovered too late. Confronted, Lena attacks Mirabel; Agnes's testimony and Wren's presence break the room open. Emotional beat: cathartic exposure—thirty years of polish cracking at once.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later, Lena confesses; the estate passes to Wren, who takes the name Juniper as her own. Mirabel declines Ambrose's retainer, files his last will for the Voss family, and opens a small practice taking cases no one else wants. Emotional beat: quiet transformation—the invisible man steps into the light, carrying what survival cost them all.
